posts.title: Can Two Walk Together?
posts.quote: Like God said, "Can two walk together except they be agreed?" If we are going to walk together with God, we must be in agreement with God.
posts.endline: We say yes to God on Sunday. → But agreement isn't a moment. It's a walk. → Can two walk together, except they be agreed? (Amos 3:3)

captions.instagram:
You can say yes to God on Sunday and still walk your own way on Monday.

That is the challenge in Amos 3:3. Walking with God is more than believing the right things. It means choosing His direction when Monday comes, when nobody is watching, and when obedience costs you something.

Ask yourself today: does the way I live agree with the God I say I follow?

Jesus did not call us to visit Him once a week. He called us to follow Him.

Sunday and Monday should look like the same person.

Amos 3:3

posts.title: Sunday and Monday Should Look Like the Same Person

captions.instagram:
Sunday and Monday should look like the same person.

It is easy to agree with God while the worship is playing and the message is being preached.

But what about Monday morning?

The real test is whether the same Jesus shapes how we speak at home, work with people, handle pressure, make decisions and treat someone who cannot do anything for us.

Agreement with God becomes visible in ordinary life.

"Can two walk together, except they be agreed?"

Amos 3:3

This week, choose one area where your Monday needs to catch up with your Sunday.

posts.title: Don't Just Preach Christ. Live Christ.
posts.quote: It is not because we preach Christ that people are getting saved, but because we live Christ.
posts.onscreen: DON'T JUST PREACH CHRIST. LIVE CHRIST.
posts.endline: Most of us can explain what we believe. → The point is simpler: people see it before they hear it. → waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God. (Romans 8:19)

captions.instagram:
People should be able to see something of Jesus before we ever tell them about Jesus.

Bishop Henry Emmanuel puts it simply:

"Not because we preach Christ, but because we live Christ."

Our words matter. But the way we respond under pressure, treat people, forgive, serve and show kindness gives those words weight.

Romans 8:19 speaks of creation waiting for the revealing of the children of God.

So here is today's challenge: let someone meet the character of Christ through the way you live.

posts.title: The Kind of Fast God Asks For
posts.quote: Is it not the type of fast I ask you to fast, that when you see the poor you attend to their needs, when you see the homeless bring them home?
posts.onscreen: THE KIND OF FAST GOD ASKS FOR
posts.endline: Fasting and prayer are good things. → But God asked for more: bread for the hungry. → Is not this the fast that I have chosen? (Isaiah 58:6)

captions.instagram:
God is not impressed by devotion that never reaches another person.

Isaiah 58 challenges a kind of fasting that looks spiritual but leaves people around us hungry, hurting and forgotten.

The fast God asks for changes more than our eating. It changes how we respond to need.

Look around you today.

Who needs food?
Who needs practical help?
Who needs to know they have not been forgotten?

Jesus continually moved towards people in need. Our devotion should move us in the same direction.

Isaiah 58:6-7

Watch the full message by searching Calvary Hephzibah on YouTube.

posts.title: What Does a Fast God Accepts Actually Look Like?

captions.instagram:
What does a fast God accepts actually look like?

Isaiah 58 gives a surprisingly practical answer.

Feed the hungry.
Welcome those in need.
Do not turn away from people who need your help.

Real devotion does not stay in the prayer room. It walks out of the door and notices people.

So make this personal.

Who near you is hungry, alone or in need this week?

Ask Jesus to open your eyes, then be willing to become part of the answer.

Isaiah 58:7

posts.title: Let No One Hurry You
posts.quote: Let no one hurry you. Let no one make you to say what God has not put in your heart.
posts.endline: We're quick to reply. Quick to react. → But pressure to answer isn't a reason to speak. → let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath. (James 1:19)

captions.instagram:
Not every question needs an immediate answer.

Not every message needs an instant reply.

And pressure to speak is not a reason to say something God has not put in your heart.

"Let no one hurry you."

James tells us to be quick to listen, slow to speak and slow to anger.

That is a powerful rhythm for today.

Listen first.
Slow down.
Then speak in a way that sounds like Jesus.

James 1:19

posts.title: Your Words Open Doors or Shut Them
posts.quote: What comes out of a man will either build you up or wreck you. What comes out of a man will either open door for you or shut the door.
posts.onscreen: YOUR WORDS OPEN DOORS OR SHUT THEM.
posts.endline: We don't always notice what our words do. → The door you shut might be your own. → Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart, be acceptable in thy sight, O LORD. (Psalm 19:14)

captions.instagram:
Some doors are opened or closed by the words we choose.

A sharp reply can damage trust in seconds. A gracious answer can change the direction of a conversation.

That is why our words are not a small part of following Jesus.

Before you speak today, ask:

Will this build or break?
Will this heal or hurt?
Would I be comfortable saying this with Jesus beside me?

"Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart, be acceptable in thy sight, O LORD."

Psalm 19:14

Before you speak, try these four things.

Listen first.
Do not prepare your reply while the other person is still talking. James 1:19.

Slow down.
You do not have to be rushed into words you will later regret.

Build up.
Ask whether what you are about to say will actually help. Ephesians 4:29.

Answer gently.
"A soft answer turneth away wrath." Proverbs 15:1.

Four simple habits. One bigger goal: let Jesus shape not only what comes out of your mouth, but the heart it comes from.

Which one do you need most today?

posts.title: True Christianity Is Self-Control
posts.quote: True Christianity, one of the things that God refer to as true Christianity, apart from taking care of the widows, is self-control.
posts.endline: We lock our doors. We guard our phones. → But do we guard our own spirit? → He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls. (Proverbs 25:28)

captions.instagram:
You protect your home. But are you guarding your own spirit?

Proverbs gives us a powerful picture of a person without self-control: a city broken down, without walls.

No protection. No boundary. Anything can get in, and anything can come out.

Following Jesus includes learning when not to react, when not to speak, when to walk away and when to bring our emotions back under His rule.

Self-control is not weakness. It is strength that has learned where to stop.

Ask Jesus to help you guard what He is building in you.

Proverbs 25:28
